summary: The enclosed track was inset 3px at the sides and 4px at the top and bottom; the sheet lays out 4px on all four. The source read symmetric — `p-[2px]`, one padding, four sides — and was not on screen: 24px rows plus 2 + 2 plus a 1.5px border the browser USES as 1px is 31, `h-8` demanded 32, and `items-center` paid the spare pixel out of the vertical gaps. A fixed height is a second author of an inset and the two agree only by arithmetic accident, so the height is gone: it is now 24 + 3 + 3 + 1 + 1 = the same 32px, derived. `items-center` is gone too, so every tab stretches to the content box and all four gaps are the padding whatever a tab contains. The inset is 3px, the sheet's own, which also closes CONVENTIONS §6 against the PADDING box (8 − 1 border = 7 = radius-sm 4 + 3) — the previous 2px never did, and the component's comment said so and shipped anyway. Second fix in the same component: the ghost strip stretched full-width and `justify-center` centred it, against both the sheet (a 280px box at x=0) and Tab's own docstring ("ghost sizes to its content and sits left"); it hugs now. Third: `doc.design` pointed at D7G-0, the Text Area artboard. The browser test that asserted `padding === "2px"` and called it "the sheet's own inset" had been written from the component rather than the design, so it pinned the drift rather than catching it — corrected, and the four-sided inset is now asserted against Paper's own world coordinates.
